text:
maria: Hey — running into a weird auth failure when CI runs `bundle install` for the redwood-ruby sampleapp. Works on my laptop but CI shows 401 for our private gem server. Anyone seen credentials just not being picked up inside a Docker-based runner?

kevin: What bundler version in CI vs local? sometimes bundler 3 changed where it reads configs.

maria: CI uses the official ruby:3.2 image and runs `gem install bundler` (no version pin). Local is bundler 2.4.x. Error snippet: 
```
Fetch https://gems.example.com/api/v1/dependencies?gems=redwood-ruby - 401 Unauthorized
An error occurred while installing redwood-ruby (0.4.1), and Bundler cannot continue.
```

samir: Two quick guesses: 1) CI user/home different so `~/.netrc` not visible, 2) bundler config key encoding for private hosts changed (`BUNDLE_...` env var names).

maria: I do set `~/.netrc` via a secrets step in the pipeline. The file is present, but bundler still fails.

kevin: Can you paste the Docker steps? if you're doing `docker build` the netrc needs to be copied during build or mounted at run time. CI sometimes strips HOME while building.

maria: Dockerfile snippet: 
```Dockerfile
FROM ruby:3.2
WORKDIR /app
COPY . /app
RUN gem install bundler && bundle config set --local path '/usr/local/bundle' && bundle install
```
We only inject netrc as a secret at runtime (not during build).

samir: There you go. `bundle install` during build won't see runtime-mounted netrc. Two options: move `bundle install` to the container start (not ideal), or inject credentials at build time via build-arg or temporary step, or use Bundler credentials via env vars.

jen: A pragmatic quick fix: pin bundler to 2 in CI build: `gem install bundler -v 2.4.11` before `bundle install`. That often matches local behavior and unblocks. But long term we should document the build-time credential requirement in the sampleapp.

maria: Pinning to bundler 2 worked — CI passed. Will open a tiny PR to note the build-time credential gotcha in the sampleapp README and add a CI job that checks `bundle install` during build with a dummy private source.

kevin: For the PR, add a note about the `BUNDLE__HOST__GEMS__COM` env var pattern too (how Bundler encodes host names into env var keys) — folks keep getting tripped up by the double underscore rules.

samir: Also include a recommended pattern snippet for CI platforms: 
```bash
# for GitHub Actions (example)
- name: Setup .netrc
  run: |
    printf "machine gems.example.com login $GEMS_USER password $GEMS_TOKEN" > ~/.netrc
    chmod 600 ~/.netrc
- name: Build image
  run: docker build --build-arg GEMS_TOKEN=$GEMS_TOKEN .
```

ci-bot: CI run 2123456900: build (rubygem/quickstart) failed -> now passing on rerun :white_check_mark:

jen: Thanks for taking this, maria. For the PR keep it tiny: README note + one-line CI tweak in the sampleapp workflow. I'll review.

maria: Opening PR now, tag: #patch/ruby-onboard-cred-readme. assigning @jen and @kevin as reviewers.

kevin: Happy to review. Might also add a small `Troubleshooting` entry in devex handbook referencing this exact scenario. :thumbsup:

maria: Great — thanks everyone!
